annotation.title_clean: Algorithmic discrimination under the AI Act and the GDPR
annotation.title_en: Algorithmic discrimination under the AI Act and the GDPR
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliamentary Research Service (De Luca, S.; Federico, M.)
annotation.venue: European Parliament Think Tank (EPRS At a Glance)
annotation.summary_en: EPRS briefing on the interplay between AI Act Article 10(5), which permits processing special categories of personal data for bias detection in high-risk AI, and the stricter GDPR Article 9. It identifies legal uncertainty and suggests legislative reform or further guidance. Autonomous cars are mentioned as one discrimination scenario.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI Act Art. 10(5) allows special-category data processing for bias detection in high-risk systems, with safeguards.
GDPR prevails over the AI Act in case of conflict.
Art. 9(2)(g) GDPR substantial public interest may serve as a legal basis.
Conditions: cybersecurity, data minimisation, strict necessity, Art. 9 grounds.
Legal uncertainty may require GDPR reform or further guidelines.
